prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but instead of naming one “best” lawyer (which depends on your injuries, goals, and preferences) here’s a practical process to find the right Pleasanton-area attorney plus what to do right now.

Immediate steps (do these first)
- Get medical treatment and follow your doctor’s instructions (creates medical records that document injury).  
- Preserve evidence: photos of damage, injuries, scene; police report number; contact info for witnesses; vehicle damage estimates; upload to cloud.  
- Notify your auto insurer (tell them facts, but avoid detailed recorded statements about fault until you talk to a lawyer).  
- Note deadlines: general personal injury lawsuit deadline in California is 2 years from the injury (California Code of Civil Procedure §335.1). Property damage is often 3 years. Claims against a government agency usually require a written claim within 6 months—so act fast if a public entity is involved.  
- Don’t sign or accept any settlement offer until you’ve had it reviewed by a lawyer.

How to choose the right injury lawyer
1. Look for the right specialization
   - Auto/personal injury and trial experience (not just traffic tickets or general practice).  
   - Experience with similar facts (e.g., multi-vehicle crash, hit-and-run, pedestrian, catastrophic injury, brain/spinal injury).

2. Verify credentials & reputation
   - Check the CA State Bar for license status and disciplinary history.  
   - Look at peer/client reviews (Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell, Google, Yelp) but weigh them with caution.  
   - Ask for references or sample verdicts/settlements for similar cases.

3. Ask about who actually handles the case
   - Will the attorney you meet do most of the work, or will paralegals/juniors handle it? Get the name of the primary contact and how often you’ll hear from them.

4. Fee structure & costs
   - Most injury lawyers work on contingency (no fee unless you recover). Typical contingency fees: ~33% pre-suit, 33–40% if the case is litigated — confirm specifics in writing.  
   - Ask who pays litigation costs (medical records, expert fees) and whether costs come out of your recovery.

5. Trial experience & case handling style
   - What percentage of their cases go to trial? (A willingness and record in court is important for leverage.)  
   - How long might your case take? What’s their strategy for maximizing recovery?

Questions to ask at a free consultation (bring your notes/photos)
- Have you handled cases like mine? What was the outcome?  
- Who will handle my file day-to-day? How often will I get updates?  
- What do you estimate the case is worth (range) and why?  
- What is your fee and what expenses would I be responsible for?  
- Do you foresee any obstacles (comparative fault, pre-existing conditions, statute of limitations)?  
- Can you provide references from past clients?

Where to find Pleasanton / Alameda County attorneys
- Alameda County Bar Association Lawyer Referral Service.  
- California State Bar’s “Find a Lawyer” or certified specialist lists.  
- Local search: Pleasanton, Dublin, Livermore, San Ramon, Walnut Creek personal injury firms (look for AV/peer-review ratings and trial records).  
- Hospital/doctor referrals (doctors often work with reliable attorneys).  
If you want, I can help generate a short list of local firms to contact and draft an email/phone script for the consultations.

Red flags to avoid
- Guarantees of a specific dollar amount or “quick cash” on first contact.  
- Pressure to sign immediately or to accept an early low offer.  
- Requests for high upfront fees or unexplained charges.  
- Attorney with little or no trial experience if your case may require litigation.

If you want next steps, tell me:
- The severity/type of your injuries and whether someone was at fault (brief summary).  
- Whether you saw a doctor and have a police report.  
- Whether you prefer a small local firm or a larger regional firm.  

I can then (a) draft a phone/email script for free consultations, or (b) compile a short list of nearby attorneys and what to look for in each.
